name: Barriere Fouquet's New York
positioning: Fouquet's New York, a Martin Brudnizki-designed hotel on Tribeca's cobblestone streets with 1930s Art Deco interiors, terrace suites, a Biologique Recherche spa and a guest and members-only rooftop
best_for: Travelers who want a Tribeca base with Parisian Art Deco design
Guests who want a suite with a private terrace or Hudson River views
Families or groups who need two- or three-bedroom connecting suites

facts.text: The hotel is on Tribeca's cobblestone streets.
The hotel's address is 456 Greenwich Street, New York, NY 10013.
The hotel was designed by Martin Brudnizki and blends 1930s Art Deco glamour, with brass, velvet and soft lighting, with an intimate, residential feel.
Martin Brudnizki dressed the room interiors with pastel tones, refined materials and Art Deco-inspired furniture.
Deluxe King Rooms are decorated in lavender and almond green, with tall windows overlooking Tribeca's historic red brick buildings.
The Fouquet's Penthouse covers 2,432 square feet over two floors.
The Hudson View Corner Suite has floor-to-ceiling windows looking onto the Hudson River.
The spa has a hydrotherapy pool, a sauna and a steam room.
Brasserie Fouquet's is an homage to Fouquet's Paris, founded in 1899 on the Champs-Élysées, reimagined in the heart of Tribeca.
The hotel's cinema, Cannes Cinema, hosts ticketed movie screenings on a seasonal basis.
The DOGPOUND Fitness Center is open 24 hours for hotel guests and members.
The hotel is dog-friendly and welcomes dogs up to 30 pounds at no charge.

highlights.text: The Tribeca Terrace Suite's living room opens onto a 500-square-foot terrace with panoramic views of the neighborhood's 19th-century brick buildings.
Fouquet's Corner Terrace Suite has water views of the Hudson River from the bedroom, living area and terrace.
Spa Fouquet's New York partners with Paris skincare brand Biologique Recherche to personalize treatments to each guest's objectives and needs.
Le Vaux is a rooftop reserved for hotel guests and members.
Titsou Bar has candlelit tables and evokes Paris in the 1920s and '30s.

considerations.text: The Le Vaux rooftop is seasonal and closes for the winter.
Valet parking is available for hotel guests at a daily charge.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing and an intimate boutique size with limited room inventory.
